It's the SetModTime after the upload has finished. Apparently OneDrive for Business will create a new version for the item then. You can see that, because 1.0 is always the time one uploaded the file and 2.0 the actual modtime of the original.

@ncw We could "maybe" send the modtime when creating the upload session as part of the request instead of uploading and then setting the modtime, see here: [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/rest-api/api/driveitem_createuploadsession#create-an-upload-session](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/onedrive/developer/rest-api/api/driveitem_createuploadsession#create-an-upload-session) ?

Nope, does not work.
I just did a quick hack and it still creates two versions 😞 
```2017/10/07 12:29:14 DEBUG : HTTP REQUEST (req 0xc04207a300)
2017/10/07 12:29:14 DEBUG : POST /_api/v2.0/drives/me/root:/TESTFILE:/upload.createSession HTTP/1.1
Host: raygina-my.sharepoint.com
User-Agent: rclone/v1.38
Content-Length: 116
Authorization: XXXX
Content-Type: application/json
Accept-Encoding: gzip

{"item":{"fileSystemInfo":{"createdDateTime":"2017-10-07T09:08:24Z","lastModifiedDateTime":"2017-10-07T09:08:24Z"}}}```
Did putting the modtime in the upload session work? That means we can lose an http transaction so that is a win even if it doesn't fix the problem.
Yes, that actually worked. Although I haven't tested it very much.

How can I as a user implement the workaround/fix @ncw mentioned two posts ago?

I'm trying to sync a few hundred gigabytes to OD, having 2X the used space isn't good haha. 

Thanks in advance.

Well, there is no workaround at the moment.
Rclone uploads the file to OneDrive for Business and afterwards sets the modification time to the modification time of the local file. Unfortunately OneDrive for Business (but NOT OneDrive Personal) creates a new version for the change of the modification time.

I haven't found a solution to prevent this, even sending the modification time together with the file also resulted into 2 versions.

I currently see only two options.
1. Disable setting the modification time after upload, so the file will have the time of the upload as modification time in OneDrive for Business
2. Talk to Microsoft about the issue.
Can you make your patch to set the modtime as part of the upload session available? I'd like to have a play with it before reporting the issue to Microsoft.

I tried setting `--no-update-modtime` and other combinations of flags in rclone, but still experienced duplicate versioning.  However, I did find a workaround to prevent it:

1. Open the settings menu by clicking on the gear symbol at the top of the OneDrive Business page.
1. Click **Site settings**.
1. Once on the Site settings page, navigate to **Site Administration > Site libraries and lists**.
1. Click **Customize "Documents"**.
1. Click **General Settings > Versioning Settings**.
1. Under **Document Version History** select the option **No versioning**.
- Note:  This will disable the creation of new file versions, but will not remove any previous versions. Your documents are safe.
7. Apply the changes by clicking **OK**.
7. Use rclone to upload or modify files.  (I also use the `--no-update-modtime` flag)
7. Restore the versioning settings after using rclone. (Optional)

I hope that this helps some users.  Also, my many thanks to @ncw and @olihey for implementing Business support. You rock!

Hi @Weropol, 

Thanks for finding that - happy to turn versioning off on my account. Will this need to be retrospectively fixed, ie delete all of those duplicate files or will that setting trash any of the old versions automatically?

Cheers

@reticentnz, no previous versions are removed, so you will have to delete them manually from **Storage Metrics** in the site settings, or use rclone to transfer the files out and then back into OneDrive again.
Any new information about this issue?
@Weropol other than turning off versioning we don't have a fix for this yet
